title: Why U.S. investors should be buying this stock
text:
Why U.S. investors should be buying this stock market pullback 'with both arms'
MARKETWATCH 8:56 AM ET 10/11/2018
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
Should I stay or should I run like crazy?
Investors no doubt have plenty of questions ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/reddit-users-have-questions-about-the- stock-market-and-we-have-the-answers-2018-02-07) after Wall Street's Wednesday meltdown, which wiped more than 800 points off the Dow , making for the worst day since February for it and the S&P . The Nasdaq saw its worst session since Brexit back in June 2016.
The selloff may have legs, judging by the looks of things this morning, while potential catalysts pile up--bond yields, the trade war, global growth worries, earnings jitters, your taxi driver telling you to sell.
But maybe none of that should matter to future retirees, who may want to recall some evergreen advice from investing legend Warren Buffett: "Be fearful when others are greedy and greedy only when others are fearful."
That leads us to our call of the day, from Reformed Broker's Josh Brown, who says savvy U.S. investors are not for scaring.
"Americans have accumulated $28.3 trillion in retirement assets, 19% of which is in 401(k) accounts ($5.3 trillion). There are 550,000 plans and 54 million participants. These dollars are coming in every month, the lower the prices for stocks, the better," said Brown in a wee-hours tweet-rant ( https://twitter.com/ReformedBroker/status/ 1050184433444237312), as he adds: "F****ing bring it."
Brown goes on to say that with 160 million Americans in the workforce and 80% of them under 54, "they're in the accumulation phase of their lives. I know you want them to panic for the clicks, but they won't. They are automated buyers of dips. It's the best thing for them."
( https://twitter.com/ReformedBroker/status/1050184433444237312 )
Understandably, not everyone may be feeling so Buffett-brave after Wednesday's drama. Blogging for CrackedMarket ( https://cracked.market/ ), Jani Ziedins says those losing sleep over this fresh volatility may want to trim position sizes to something that is more manageable.
Read:How much of your 401(k) retirement plan is affected by market volatility? ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how- much-of-your-401k-retirement-plan-is-affected-by-market-volatility-2018-02-16)
"The key to surviving the market is keeping your head when everyone else is losing theirs. Do whatever is necessary to reclaim your perspective. If that means dialing back your position sizes, then that is what you need to do," says Ziedins.
So if you think a 0.25% bump in Treasury rates will clobber the economy, then sell and lock-in profits, but if you don't think the economy is "teetering on the verge of a recession," ignore the noise and wait for prices go up, he says.
As for Ziedins himself: "If I wasn't already fully invested in this market, I would be buying this dip with both arms."
Read:Why the stock market ushered in its worst start to a quarter in about 2 years ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ why-the-stock-market-tumbled-wednesday-ushering-in-its-worst-start-to-a-quarter-in-about-2-years-2018-10-10)
The quote
( https://twitter.com/foxnews/status/1050234033983098880?s=12 )
"The Fed is going wild. I don't know what their problem is, but they're raising interest rates and it's ridiculous."-- That was U.S. President Trump on Fox News late Wednesday, after making similar comments ( http://www.marketwatch.com/ story/trump-says-the-fed-has-gone-crazy-after-the-dow-tumbles-830-points-in-one-day-2018-10-10) at a rally in Pennsylvania earlier in the day.
Some say, he's right, ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/why-one-economist-says-trump-is-right-about-the-fed-2018-10- 10) ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/why-one-economist-says-trump-is-right-about-the-fed-2018-10-10 ) and the Fed needs to cool it ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-fed-needs-to-stop-at-3-morici-says-2018-10-10 ), while Mohamed El-Erian ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mohamed-el-erian-stock-market-rout-will-not-derail-further-fed-rate-hikes-2018-10-10 ) says don't count on a market rout derailing the Fed. In any case, here's what Trump's tirade means for the markets ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/what-trumps-tirade-against-loco-fed-means-for-the-markets-2018-10-11 ) (http:// www.marketwatch.com/story/what-trumps-tirade-against-loco-fed-means-for-the-markets-2018-10-11)
The market
No dip buyers rushing in just yet, with Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures swinging around, but still in the red.
Crude is down, and the dollar is off, with gold up. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note has eased back to 3.15% .
Check out the Market Snapshot column ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-futures-down-more-than-200-points-as-wall- street-looks-to-build-on-losses-2018-10-11) for the latest action.
Around the globe ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/global-markets-tumble-us-stock-futures-point-to-continued-selloff- on-wall-street-2018-10-11), bears have mauled Europe and Asia, where the Shanghai Composite skidded over 5% (http:// www.marketwatch.com/story/nikkei-drops-about-4-as-asian-markets-follow-wall-streets-plunge-2018-10-10) and the Nikkei dropped near 4%.
( https://twitter.com/srussolillo/status/1050241129843544065 )
Not to be left out, bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies are getting pummeled.
Read: Dr. Doom says bitcoin represents the 'mother of all bubbles' ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dr-doom-says- bitcoin-represents-the-mother-of-all-bubbles-2018-10-10)

The buzz
While POTUS tosses shade at the Fed, it doesn't seem that Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin feels exactly the same. " Markets go up. Markets go down," he said in a Bali interview on the sidelines of an IMF meeting (https:// edition.cnn.com/2018/10/11/business/mnuchin-trump-fed-markets/index.html).
Big tech names are taking more heat this morning, led by Amazon (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Netflix (NFLX). Meanwhile, Apple has scooped up engineers from European chip maker Dialog (DLG.XE) in a $600 million deal ( https://www.wsj.com/articles/ apple-swoops-up-engineers-from-key-supplier-as-it-bolsters-in-house-chip-design-1539247647).
Shares of Square Inc. were down hard in premarket after news late Wednesday that Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar is leaving the payments firm ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/square-stock-falls-as-cfo-plans-to-leave-for-nextdoor- ceo-post-2018-10-10) to become chief executive at social-networking site Nextdoor.
We're a day away from big bank earnings, with JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Citigroup (C) and Wells Fargo (WFC) on tap. But while investors are crossing their fingers for good news, that may be a tall order ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ third-quarter-earnings-from-the-big-banks-may-not-light-a-fire-under-stocks-2018-10-08).
Read: Here's why you should expect more 'beats' during this earning season ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres- why-you-should-expect-more-beats-during-this-earnings-season-2018-10-10)
Tesla (TSLA) could be active after a judge refused to OK a settlement between CEO Elon Musk and the SEC, saying he wants both parties to explain themselves ( https://twitter.com/SamAntar/status/1050250921387745280?s=19 ). Musk also dismissed the idea that he's leaning toward outgoing Fox (FOXA) chief exec. James Murdoch as new chairman. (http:// www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musk-denies-james-murdoch-is-favorite-to-become-tesla-chairman-2018-10-10)
As Micron Technology (MU) shares get crushed by this selloff, CEO Sanjay Mehrotra tells MarketWatch (http:// www.marketwatch.com/story/micron-ceo-memory-chip-market-is-structurally-different-in-post-pc-world-2018-10-10) that a huge influx of devices that need memory and storage chips is driving demand like never before.
Consumer price data ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/housing-costs-nudge-inflation-higher-in-september-cpi-shows- 2018-10-11) came in slower than forecast, while weekly jobless claims ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/jobless-claims- fall-slightly-to-203000-and-stick-to-49-year-low-2018-09-13). The Federal budget is due later.
The stat
19 hours--That's how long 161 passengers and 13 crew will be in the air for the world's longest nonstop flight between Singapore and New York, operated by Singapore Airlines that takes off Thursday. It will be the first journey for the new, fuel efficient Airbus A350-900ULR, which has been loaded with 1,200 hours of audiovisual content.
